1: SHM occurs when the restoring force is proportional to displacement and opposite to it, so acceleration is −ω²x. This is why the period depends only on the system's properties, not on the amplitude.
2: On a displacement–time graph the gradient gives velocity, and on a velocity–time graph the gradient gives acceleration. The graphs are sinusoidal, so the phase relationships follow from the derivatives.
3: Energy transfer from the driver is most efficient when its frequency matches the natural frequency, so the amplitude grows large. Damping reduces the peak and shifts it to a lower frequency.
4: A gravitational field is the region where a mass experiences a force. Field strength is force per unit mass, and it follows Newton's law of gravitation, so it falls off with the square of distance.
5: The Hubble constant gives the rate of expansion, so its inverse estimates the age of the universe. Redshift of distant galaxies is the evidence that space itself is expanding.
